title: At the Doctor's
author: Léxi
desc: Expliquer où on a mal et comprendre le médecin.

p: Aminata is in London for her studies. One morning, she wakes up and she doesn't feel well. Her head hurts. She is hot. She goes to the doctor.
"Hello. I have an appointment at ten o'clock. My name is Aminata Koné."
"Please sit down," says the receptionist. "The doctor will see you in five minutes."
The doctor is a tall woman with glasses. "Good morning, Aminata. What's the problem?"
"I have a headache, and I have a fever. I think I'm sick."
"Do you have a sore throat? Do you cough?"
"Yes, my throat hurts a little. And I cough at night."
"Let me check," says the doctor. "Open your mouth, please. Say 'Aaah'."
"OK. Now take a deep breath. And again."
The doctor listens to her chest. She takes her temperature. "Thirty-eight point five. You have a fever. It's a bad cold, or the flu. It's not serious."
"Yes. Take one tablet three times a day, after meals. Drink a lot of water and rest. Don't go to class for two days."
"Thank you, doctor. Can I have a paper for my school?"
"Of course. Here you are. Get well soon!"

*I don't feel well.* — Je ne me sens pas bien.
*My … hurts.* — J'ai mal à…  (my head, my stomach, my back, my tooth)
*I have a fever / a cold / a cough.* — J'ai de la fièvre / un rhume / de la toux.
*Since yesterday.* — Depuis hier.
*Is it serious?* — C'est grave ?
*How many times a day?* — Combien de fois par jour ?
*Get well soon!* — Bon rétablissement !
Practise: tell a friend where it hurts, in English. "My stomach hurts since this morning."
